systems.name: Cycle-Indexed Voice-Leading System
systems.summary: The central organizational system of the Almanac: every tertian and quartal sonority is cataloged across six cycles (2-7) within three parent scales, with voice-leading analyzed at three levels for both Close and Spread voicings.

traversal_rules.name: M.S.R.P. Top-Voice Minimization
traversal_rules.summary: When traversing cycles within a parent scale, select the voicing path that produces the most stepwise melodic motion in the top voice, as indicated by the M.S.R.P. string for each cycle entry.

traversal_rules.name: Common-Tone Preference Per Voice
traversal_rules.summary: Within each cycle traversal, prefer to sustain (or minimally displace) the voice that carries a common tone between adjacent chords, minimizing aggregate voice motion across the cycle.

references.quote_excerpt: intervallic voice-leading relationships, functional voice-leading information

traversal_rules.name: Six-Cycle by Three-Scale Grid Traversal
traversal_rules.summary: Every voicing family is traversed through all 18 environments (6 cycles x 3 parent scales), making cycle and scale independent traversal axes that can be varied orthogonally.

systems.name: Voicing Family Parallelism System
systems.summary: The Almanac applies identical analytical layers to every sonority family - triads, seventh chords, TBN constructs (Vol 1), and quartal/cluster voicings (Vol 2) - in both Close and Spread positions, asserting that voice-leading is the same problem regardless of the chord family in use.

members.name: Spread Position
members.summary: Voicings expanded beyond close range; the complementary axis of the Close/Spread parameterization.

modification_rules.name: Uniform Analytical Layers Across Families
modification_rules.summary: Every voicing family - regardless of whether it is tertian, TBN, or quartal/cluster - receives the same three analytical layers: Intervallic Voice-Leading, Functional Voice-Leading, and M.S.R.P. This uniform treatment asserts that the voice-leading problem is identical across families; only the distribution of common tones, steps, and leaps differs.

references.quote_excerpt: intervallic voice-leading relationships, functional voice-leading information, and Most Stepwise Resolution Pattern (M.S.R.P.) strings
Intervallic Voice-Leading (pitch relationships), Functional Voice-Leading (harmonic context)

modification_rules.name: Close to Spread Density Axis
modification_rules.summary: Each voicing family entry is fully parameterized along the Close/Spread axis: the same chord in close position and spread position is cataloged as a pair, allowing the density of any voicing to be modified while preserving the underlying intervallic and functional voice-leading analysis.

references.quote_excerpt: Each voicing is displayed in both close and spread positions
3-part and 4-part quartal voicings (close, spread, and cluster formations)

modification_rules.name: Quartal / Cluster NCT Harmonization - Resist Naming
modification_rules.summary: Vol 2 quartal and cluster voicings are explicitly treated as sonorities that resist conventional chord naming. The analytical layers are applied identically, but the harmonic identity is left open - these voicings harmonize non-chord tones by embedding them in structures that do not privilege any single tonal interpretation.

references.quote_excerpt: the volume's strategic shift away from tertian harmony toward quartal and cluster sonorities that resist conventional chord naming

systems.name: Three-Layer Analytical System
systems.summary: The Almanac imposes three mandatory analytical lenses on every voicing entry: Intervallic Voice-Leading (which voice moves by which interval), Functional Voice-Leading (which scale-degree function moves to which), and M.S.R.P. (the most stepwise top-voice path through the cycle). These layers are the book's primary teaching mechanism, replacing prose explanation with exhaustive, machine-readable mappings.

members.name: Intervallic Voice-Leading
members.summary: Maps each voice's motion to a specific interval (unison, 2nd, 3rd, etc.) between successive chords in the cycle.

members.name: Functional Voice-Leading
members.summary: Maps each voice's motion in terms of scale-degree function (root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, etc.) - the harmonic grammar layer above raw intervals.

members.name: M.S.R.P. (Most Stepwise Resolution Pattern)
members.summary: A string encoding the most stepwise form of the top-voice melodic line through the complete cycle, serving as a melodic efficiency benchmark for voice-leading choices.

traversal_rules.name: Intervallic Voice Motion Mapping
traversal_rules.summary: For each step in a cycle traversal, the intervallic layer is read first to identify which voice carries the common tone (interval 0), which voices move by step (intervals 1-2), and which voices must leap - establishing the motion budget before any voicing is chosen.

traversal_rules.name: Functional Layer Substitution Expansion
traversal_rules.summary: Because the functional layer tracks scale-degree function independently of the specific chord, voicings sharing identical functional voice-leading profiles across different cycles or scales are interchangeable substitutes - the functional layer is the basis for any substitution logic built on top of the catalog.
